source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 3. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: Ṭahārah means being clean and pure. It has two sides: a hidden state called ḥadath, and a thing you can see called najāsah.
learn.title: Two sides of purity

learn.en: Ḥadath is a state you are in — you cannot see it. Small ḥadath is removed by wudu. Big ḥadath is removed by ghusl, a full bath.
learn.title: Ḥadath: a hidden state

learn.en: Najāsah is a thing on you, like urine. You remove it by washing it away.
learn.title: Najāsah: a thing you wash off

learn.en: If there is no water, or you cannot use it, you do tayammum: you strike clean earth with your hands and wipe your face and hands. (Qur'an 5:6)
learn.title: No water? Tayammum

learn.en: These break wudu: passing urine, passing stool, passing wind, and deep sleep. After them, make wudu again before you pray.
learn.title: What breaks wudu

learn.en: Allah loves people who keep clean: “Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves.” (Qur'an 2:222)
learn.title: Allah loves the clean

words.en: a state that needs wudu or ghusl

quiz.en: What do we do if there is no water?
True or false? Passing wind breaks wudu.
True or false? Deep sleep breaks wudu.
True or false? You can see ḥadath on your clothes.

think.q: You woke up from a deep nap and it's time for Asr. Do you need wudu? Why?
think.a: Yes — deep sleep breaks wudu, so make wudu, then pray Asr.

parents.summary: Ṭahārah means removing ḥadath (by wudu, ghusl or tayammum) and removing najāsah (by washing). Urine, stool, wind and deep sleep break wudu.
parents.tip: After a nap or the toilet, ask: “Do you still have wudu?” — make it a habit.
